title: fix: stop polli gen text waiting forever on open stdin
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fix `polli gen text "<prompt>"` hanging with no output when the caller leaves stdin open (Node `exec`/`spawn`, agent harnesses, CI runners)
- With a prompt argument, stdin is optional context: wait up to 3 s for the first byte, then continue without it (`< /dev/null` skips the wait)
- Without an argument, stdin is the prompt and is read to EOF as before
- Same approach as Gemini CLI (500 ms) and Claude Code (3 s); bumps the CLI to 0.1.18

| Caller | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Open socket/pipe + prompt argument | hangs forever | runs after 3 s |
| `cat file \| polli gen text "q"` | file as context | unchanged |
| `echo hi \| polli gen text` | prompt from stdin | unchanged |

Verified: the new test fails on main; the built CLI with the socketpair repro from #15518 sends its request after 3.5 s.

Fixes #15518

gist.headline: The pipe can wait
gist.blurb: Polli no longer waits forever for stdin that might never say hello. Give `polli gen text` a prompt, and it gets on with the job after three seconds.
gist.summary: Polli CLI 0.1.18 lets `polli gen text "<prompt>"` proceed after waiting up to 3 seconds for optional stdin context, while preserving piped context and stdin-only prompts.
gist.impact: Calls from Node processes, agent harnesses, and CI runners with an open stdin pipe now send their request instead of hanging; piped input still works as before.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the Polli CLI as a cozy retro terminal. An open pipe and a small three-second timer show the former wait; Polli taps the send key while a CRT robot watches the request go through. Add a code-plant beside the terminal.
